newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM formally appoints new cabinet ministers.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM formally appoints new cabinet ministers.

text.p: Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto appointed new ministers for his cabinet on Thursday, placing veterans to manage Japan's economic, trade and foreign policies.

Hiroshi Mitsuzuka, 69, was appointed to head the powerful Finance Ministry, Chief Cabinet Secretary Seiroku Kajiyama told reporters. The ministry faces drastic reforms after causing public uproar for the way it handled problems in the banking system and for scandals involving senior officials.
Mitsuzuka held a number of key posts in the cabinet and in the Liberal Democratic Party in the 1980s, including a brief stint as foreign minister and a longer spell as trade minister.
Mitsuzuka leads one of the biggest LDP factions.

Shinji Sato, a veteran lawmaker with an elite political pedigree, was appointed to head the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI). He served as transport minister in 1988 and is the son of former prime minister Eisaku Sato, who was Japan's longest-serving prime minister.
Taro Aso was appointed chief of the Economic Planning Agency (EPA), which is responsible for the study and research of economic matters.

Yukihiko Ikeda is to continue serving as foreign minister to handle pending foreign policy issues, such as cementing a new security arrangement with the United States and mending ties with China about a row over disputed islands.
Ikeda has served as head of the Management and Coordination Agency and the defence agency.

Hashimoto was re-elected prime minister by the parliament earlier today. Hashimoto will lead a minority government after his conservative LDP failed to win a majority in a general election last month and then failed to renew the outgoing three-party coalition.
The new cabinet consists entirely of LDP members, the first time in three years the party has monopolised the cabinet.
